name: Supervised Tutoring in Class
title: Supervised Tutoring in Class
answer: Supervised tutoring in class means students use a school configured AI tutor while the teacher stays in the room, watching who is stuck, who is moving ahead, and who is using the tool to avoid thinking. It matters because the teacher's presence is what makes AI tutoring work, and the tool extends the teacher's reach during practice rather than replacing the lesson.

sections.body: This idea places AI tutoring inside the classroom with a teacher present rather than leaving students alone with a tool. Students work with a tutor the school has set up, such as a configured account in Gemini for Education, while the teacher moves around the room. The teacher can then see who is stuck, who is racing ahead, and who is using the tool to avoid thinking. The problem it solves is that tutoring without supervision can let students drift, accept wrong answers, or skip the thinking entirely. The teacher's presence is described as what made the Nigerian trial work.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, the teacher first teaches a concept, then gives a short period of tutored practice, and finally brings the class back together to discuss what was learned. During the practice period, students work with the school configured tutor while the teacher circulates and observes. The tool should follow hint only instructions, asking what the student has tried and guiding one step at a time, and it should be given the correct answers and common mistakes for the lesson. Students can work in pairs, which lets them talk through problems with each other as well as with the tool, and a pair can catch a tutor's error that one student might accept. The text does not give separate grade band versions of this practice.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text labels this idea through the Nigerian trial and the Nigerian program. Teachers in the Nigerian program received three days of training before the sessions began (De Simone et al., 2025). The text states that the teacher's presence is what made the Nigerian trial work, and that students in the Nigerian program worked in pairs. No other study, figure or finding is given in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The tool should follow hint only instructions, asking what the student has tried and guiding one step at a time, rather than giving answers away. It should be given the correct answers and common mistakes for the lesson so its guidance stays accurate. A pair can catch a tutor's error that one student might accept, which is one reason pairing is safer than working alone. Supervised tutoring works best as part of a lesson, not a replacement for one, and the teacher still does the teaching. The decisions about setup, lesson design and when to intervene stay with the teacher.
